body.statement: Suppose \(J\ge2\), \(H>0\), \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).  For the frozen local face space, whose effect vector \(b\) is unrestricted, \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty\).  More precisely, there are two donor-switch faces at any sufficiently small score separation \(c\in(0,H]\) such that every honest confidence kernel has worst-face expected diameter at least \(\Delta[1-2\alpha-v_c]\) for every \(\Delta>0\), where \(v_c=2\Phi(\rho_c/2)-1\), \(\rho_c\to0\) as \(c\downarrow0\), is the total-variation distance between the two Gaussian laws.  Thus the least-favorable two-point sequence escapes through \(\Delta\to\infty\), and the requested finite-valued frontier and finite attaining program do not exist on \(\mathcal H_H\) as defined; a finite formulation must additionally bound the effect spread or otherwise restrict \(b\).
body.proof_tex:
Choose distinct labels \(1,2\) and a unit vector \(e\in\mathbb R^q\).  For \(0<c\le H\), define two score vectors by
\[
 h^{(0)}_1=0,\quad h^{(0)}_j=ce\ (j\ne1),
 \qquad
 h^{(1)}_2=0,\quad h^{(1)}_j=ce\ (j\ne2).
\]
For an arbitrary \(\Delta>0\), use in both states the same effect vector
\[
 b^{(\Delta)}_1=0,\qquad b^{(\Delta)}_2=\Delta,
 \qquad b^{(\Delta)}_j=0\quad(j>2).
\]
Each parameter lies in \(\mathcal H_H\): its score norms do not exceed \(H\), it has exactly one zero label, and the coherence restriction is therefore satisfied.  Their targets are respectively
\(
 \tau(h^{(0)},b^{(\Delta)})=0
\)
and
\(
 \tau(h^{(1)},b^{(\Delta)})=\Delta
\).

Let \(m_0\) and \(m_1\) be the corresponding interleaved means of \(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}\), and set
\(
 \rho_c=\|\Omega^{-1/2}(m_1-m_0)\|_2
\).
Only the first two score blocks differ, linearly in \(c\), so \(\rho_c\to0\) as \(c\downarrow0\).  For two normals with common covariance, direct likelihood-ratio integration gives
\[
 \|N(m_0,\Omega)-N(m_1,\Omega)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =2\Phi(\rho_c/2)-1=:v_c.
\tag{15}
\]
Indeed, after whitening and projecting onto the direction of the mean difference, the likelihood ratio crosses one at the midpoint; the difference of the two half-space probabilities is
\(\Phi(\rho_c/2)-\Phi(-\rho_c/2)\), which is (15).

Let \(K\) be any kernel satisfying the honesty constraint in Definition \(\mathrm{def:gaussian\text{-}minimax\text{-}risk}\), and define
\(
 A_0=\{0\in K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}})\}
\)
and
\(
 A_1=\{\Delta\in K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}})\}
\).
Writing \(P_0,P_1\) for the two Gaussian laws, honesty and the definition of total variation imply
\[
 P_0(A_0)\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 P_0(A_1)\ge P_1(A_1)-v_c\ge1-\alpha-v_c.
\]
Therefore
\[
 P_0(A_0\cap A_1)\ge1-2\alpha-v_c.
\]
On the intersection the confidence set contains points separated by \(\Delta\), so
\[
 \sup_{(h,b)\in\mathcal H_H}
 \mathbb E_{h,b,\Omega}[\operatorname{diam}(K(Z^{\mathrm{pan}}))]
 \ge\Delta[1-2\alpha-v_c].
\tag{16}
\]
Because \(\alpha<1/2\) and \(v_c\to0\), choose a fixed \(c\in(0,H]\) with \(v_c<1-2\alpha\).  The bracket in (16) is then a strictly positive constant independent of \(\Delta\).  Letting \(\Delta\to\infty\), which is allowed because Definition \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}face\text{-}space}\) does not bound \(b\), shows that every honest kernel has infinite worst-case expected diameter.  Taking the infimum over kernels proves \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty\).  The two-point families indexed by \(\Delta\) are the promised explicit generic-class certificate.
